summary: Albert Lutz is a historian, archaeologist, and sinologist. He studied at the University of Zurich (~1975–1985) under Eberhard Fischer and served as curator of Chinese art (1982) and director (1998–2019) at Museum Rietberg.

Albert Schweitzer was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Strasbourg (~1893–1913) under Wilhelm Deecke, the University of Tübingen (~1899), and the German University of Prague, later holding a post at Strasbourg (~1902–1912).
Albert Sechehaye was a linguist. He studied at the University of Geneva (~1888–1893) and under Ferdinand de Saussure (~1893–1898), subsequently working at the University of Geneva from ~1903 to 1945.

Albert Thumb was a linguist who studied under Karl Brugmann, Hermann Osthoff, and Rudolf Thurneysen, and at the Seminar for Oriental Languages and University of Freiburg. He held posts at Freiburg (1891, 1895), Marburg (~1901–1909), and Strasbourg (1909).

Albert Welter is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at McMaster University (~1980–1987) under Koichi Shinohara, Yün-hua Jan, and Ryosho Tanaka, and held posts at the University of Winnipeg (~1993–2013) and University of Arizona (2013).
Alberto Todeschini is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He has held posts as a guest at Kyoto University and at the Italian School of East Asian Studies (attested 2010).

Albion Moonlight Butters is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Harvard University, the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and Columbia University (PhD 2006) under Robert A. F. Thurman and numerous other academic and traditional teachers.

Albrecht Hanisch is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Marburg (PhD 2000) under Michael Hahn and held posts at the Nepal Research Centre (attested 2013–2018) and the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project (attested 2018).

Albrecht Weber was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Breslau, Bonn, and Berlin under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler, Christian Lassen, Johann Gildemeister, and Adalbert Kuhn, and held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (1848, 1851–1852, 1856, 1867–1901).

Albrecht Wezler was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tübingen (~1960–1965) under Paul Thieme. He held posts at the University of Hamburg (1973–2003) and the Nepal Research Centre (1982–2004), among other institutions.

Aleix Ruiz-Falqués is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Cambridge (2016) under Eivind Kahrs, and held posts at Shan State Buddhist University (2019) and the Pali Text Society (2026).

Aleksander Brückner was a linguist, historian, and archaeologist. He studied at the University of Lviv, University of Vienna, and Frederick William University Berlin under August Leskien, later holding posts at the University of Lviv (~1878–1881) and Berlin (~1881–1924).
Alessandro Giudice is an Indologist. He has held posts at the University of Munich (attested 2026) and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Alessandro Graheli is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He has held positions at the University of Vienna (attested 2022), the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2022), and the University of Toronto (attested 2026).

Alex McKay is a historian, archaeologist, and Tibetologist who completed his PhD at SOAS University of London in 1995. He held fellowships at SOAS, University College London, and the International Institute for Asian Studies.

Alex Watson is an Indology and philosophy scholar. Educated at Oxford and SOAS, he studied under Alexis Sanderson, Harunaga Isaacson, and Ernst Steinkellner, and held posts at Wolfson College, Oxford (2006), Harvard University, and Ashoka University (2018–2020).

Alex Wayman was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at UCLA and UC Berkeley under Ferdinand Lessing and Murray Barnson Emeneau, later holding posts at UC Berkeley (~1957–1961), Wisconsin-Madison (~1961–1967), and Columbia University (1967–1991).

Alexander Berzin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rutgers, Princeton, and Harvard (PhD ~1965–1972) under Masatoshi Nagatomi and several Tibetan teachers, and worked at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (~1972–1998).

Alexander Coburn Soper was an art historian, archaeologist, sinologist, and japanologist. He studied at Hamilton College and Princeton University, worked as an editor for Artibus Asiae (1958–1993), and was a professor at New York University (1960).

Alexander Cunningham was an archaeologist and Indologist. He studied at Christ's Hospital, Addiscombe Military Seminary, and under James Prinsep; he later served as archaeological surveyor (1861–1865) and Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1861–1865; 1871–1885).
